findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging (println!), allocation, and domain Record construction in a single function. Data/Calculations/Actions separation is violated.
findings.failure_mode: I/O and logging are embedded in data construction, making the function impossible to test deterministically and preventing pure calculation reuse.
findings.fix: Split into shell function (reads file and logs) and pure calculation function (parses lines into Records). Return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() discards the Result and panics on any file I/O error.
findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission denied, or I/O error causes a panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and propagate fs::read_to_string error with ?.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console logging in the data-parsing path. Logging is a shell-side effect.
findings.failure_mode: Side-effectful output is produced during domain data construction, making the function non-deterministic and untestable.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing path. Move any logging to the shell layer outside the pure calculation.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use direct indexing without bounds checking. Malformed lines with fewer than 2 fields cause panic.
findings.failure_mode: A single line missing a comma or with only one field panics the entire program at runtime.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') and handle the None case with a typed Invalid error. Access only validated fields.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value in the second field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric input (e.g., 'abc') aborts the entire packet load instead of producing a typed parse error for that record.
findings.fix: Use map_err to convert ParseIntError into a typed ParseError::Invalid for the record.

findings.problem: (parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) silently truncates any value > 65535 from u32 to u16.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u16 range value (0-65535) parsed as u32 is fine, but any u32 value > 65535 silently wraps, silently corrupting data.
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16, or use u32::try_into().map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) for checked conversion.

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper. All failure modes (I/O, parse, overflow) are collapsed into panic surfaces.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between file-not-found, invalid format, or out-of-range values. No graceful recovery is possible.
findings.fix: Define an enum ParseError { Io(io::Error), EmptyLine, Invalid(String), Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> allocates without any capacity bound or domain max. No try_reserve.
findings.failure_mode: A very large file or extremely long lines cause unbounded heap allocation, potentially OOM.
findings.fix: Validate line count against a domain cap before iterating. Use try_reserve on the output Vec after validating the cap.

findings.problem: Uses split(',').map().collect() producing intermediate Vec<String> instead of mandatory split_once(',') for one-separator grammars.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary intermediate allocation per line. Extra allocations waste memory and CPU cycles in a parsing hot path.
findings.fix: Use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; then parse value_str.trim().

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String. Domain names carry rules (non-empty, trimmed) but the type has no enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct Record { name: "" , ... } or Record { name: "  ", ... }, violating domain invariants silently.
findings.fix: Use a Name newtype with a smart constructor: pub struct Name(String); impl Name { fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> { ... } }

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String slices from split) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: The function accepts hostile input, processes it with unchecked indexing, and produces Records that may contain empty names or out-of-range values.
findings.fix: Parse all raw input through fallible smart constructors at the boundary. Core logic should only consume validated domain types.

findings.problem: Record has pub name: String and pub value: u16. No encapsulation or validation on mutation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mutate name to empty string or value to arbitrary u16, breaking domain invariants after construction.
findings.fix: Make fields private or derive Copy/Clone, remove setters, and enforce validity at construction via smart constructors.

findings.problem: No tests exist in the crate. No test targets, no #[cfg(test)] module, no behavior verification.
findings.failure_mode: No evidence that the function works correctly for valid input, empty files, malformed lines, missing files, or out-of-range values.
findings.fix: Add a tests module with cases: valid input, empty file, missing file, malformed line, overflow value, and extra fields.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the packet-loading hot path. Performance is unmeasured.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify if the unbounded intermediate Vec allocations or per-line String allocations are a bottleneck. No baseline for optimization decisions.
findings.fix: Add criterion or tinytemplate benchmarks measuring allocations, throughput (records/sec), and latency for typical and hostile input sizes.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied packet-loading performance
no profiler data for allocation hot spots in load_packets
no allocation budget or try_reserve usage anywhere in the crate
no command evidence: cargo test, cargo clippy, or cargo fmt were not run
no behavior tests exist to verify correct parsing, error handling, or boundary cases
residual_risk: Static review identifies 12 violations including 8 blockers: hidden I/O fused in pure logic, multiple panic surfaces (unwrap on I/O, parse, indexing), lossy u32-to-u16 cast, no typed error taxonomy, unbounded allocation, missing parse boundary, raw primitive domain fields, and absent tests. The function cannot be safely used without rewriting to follow Data/Calculations/Actions separation, returning typed errors, eliminating all panic surfaces, and adding bounded allocation with try_reserve.
